matrixClaims.statement: checkout HEAD is the pinned commit
every MANIFEST.json artifact digest and byte length matches the checkout
MANIFEST, expected.json and report.json all carry contract 1.0.1
committed report.json sha256 equals the value in the d90e5d3 cold-run packet
every expected block in report.json equals expected.json
the matrix README case table states the same outcome as expected.json for every case
matrixClaims.note: documentation consistency only; does not affect any computed result

authorizationClaims.statement: EIP-712 digest recomputed by hand from the 2.1 field list, 2.3 path map and domain {PriorSeal, 2, intent.chainId}
authorizationClaims.ruleSource: EIP-712 (standard), with the field list of INPUT-CONTRACT.md 2.1 and 2.3
authorizationClaims.note: typeString=PriorSealAuthorization(bytes32 intentHash,string principalType,string principalId,address principalAccount,string authorizerType,address authorizer,string agentId,address executor,uint256 issuedAt,uint256 notBefore,uint256 expiresAt,bytes32 authorizationNonce,uint256 maxUses,string audience,bytes32 policyHash); domainType=EIP712Domain(string name,string version,uint256 chainId); domainSeparator=0x9ed60ffc78d5f51ee92451b9443adf92acd3513347808e4b1a824222a802c9e1; structHash=0xf5cafd21b6c6e911544a06361fbb5b7b8511e33b051a7c7d05a6931d8d187461

authorizationClaims.statement: signer recovered from (digest, authorization.signature) equals authorization.authorizer.address and the published test address
a second path (eth-account encode_typed_data + recover_message) yields the same digest and signer
Ed25519 signature over UTF-8(canonical JSON of acceptance without signature) verifies under the published issuer key
authorizationClaims.ruleSource: INPUT-CONTRACT.md (1.0.1) 2.2 + docs/architecture/aps-priorseal-signing-bytes-v0.4.0.md (written for a different fixture; applied here) (canonical form)

authorizationClaims.statement: acceptance issuer, keyId and algorithm match fixture/public-test-keys.json
acceptance is an ACCEPTED priorseal.authorization-receipt.v1, first log entry (sequence 1, previousEntryHash null)
authorizationClaims.ruleSource: docs/architecture/aps-priorseal-signing-bytes-v0.4.0.md (written for a different fixture; applied here); docs/architecture/lifecycle.md

authorizationClaims.statement: at reference time tRef = notBefore the authorization is inside [notBefore, expiresAt], was issued no later than notBefore, accepted inside its window, and is a single-use eip712 v2 authorization for this profile
authorizationClaims.ruleSource: docs/runs/priorseal-exact-call-matrix-v1.0.1-cold-run/README.md at d90e5d3 (authorization check at notBefore); INPUT-CONTRACT.md (1.0.1) 2
authorizationClaims.note: the reference time is not stated in INPUT-CONTRACT.md at 2ff89d8 (spec gap G2); policyHash is the zero hash and no policy document is published, so policy admission is not checked

authorizationClaims.statement: the published TEST seed and TEST secp256k1 value derive the published Ed25519 key and authorizer address
authorizationClaims.note: informational; shows the key file is self-consistent, adds nothing to signature validity

authorizationClaims.statement: EIP-55 checksum form of the recovered signer equals the published form

equality of decimal-string forms, when signed present
observed time earlier than notBefore or greater than expiresAt

claims.statement: observation is a priorseal.execution-observation.v1 envelope
observation correlates to the authorization by chain, delegated executor (authorization.delegate.executor vs observed sender) and nonce
claims.note: the observation carries no authorizationId or intentHash; the pairing itself is by fixture layout (spec gap G5)

claims.statement: acceptance.acceptedAt is not later than the observed execution time (else AUTHORIZATION_AFTER_EXECUTION)
binding to separate decision evidence
claims.note: the matrix contains no decision-evidence object and the intent carries no contextCommitments; the only pre-execution evidence is the issuer acceptance (A1 to A10)

limits: Synthetic, offline fixtures: no chain observation, no RPC, no real execution or finality.
Answer-exposed: expected.json and report.json were read before and while writing this reader.
Compliance and outcome rules are inferred from lifecycle.md prose; the contract publishes them only per case.
Hash identities (intentHash, authorizationId, authorizationHash, entryHash) use rules from a doc written for a different fixture.
Not adoption, endorsement, integration or pilot by any party. Written by a different project (HORIZON SHIELD / NENRIN).
